title: A Literature Review of the Effects of Natural Light on Building Occupants
review_question: To compile a listing of commonly cited literature showing the impacts of daylighting in buildings.
inclusion_exclusion_criteria: Literature from books, periodicals, Internet articles, and interviews commonly citing impacts of daylighting; no critical review of scientific nature was performed.

findings.antecedent: Daylighting in buildings
findings.consequent: Higher productivity, lower absenteeism, fewer errors or defects, positive attitudes, reduced fatigue, reduced eyestrain
findings.quote: Daylighting has been associated with higher productivity, lower absenteeism, fewer errors or defects in products, positive attitudes, reduced fatigue, and reduced eyestrain.

findings.antecedent: Most electrical light sources (cool white fluorescent, incandescent, energy-efficient fluorescent)
findings.consequent: Spectral distribution needed for complete biological functions (lack blue portion)
findings.quote: Most electrical light sources lack the spectral distribution needed for complete biological functions...

findings.antecedent: Full-spectrum fluorescent lighting
findings.consequent: Similarity to natural light spectrum (provides blue portion)
findings.quote: full-spectrum fluorescent lighting is the electrical light source that has a spectrum of light most similar to natural light...

findings.antecedent: Natural light
findings.consequent: Balanced spectrum of color, energy peaking in blue-green area, levels of light for biological functions (290-770 nm range, Vitamin D synthesis, tanning, bilirubin degradation)
findings.quote: Daylight provides a better lighting environment... because sunlight consists of a balanced spectrum of color...

findings.antecedent: Natural views (meadows, mountains, vegetation, water)
findings.consequent: Stress-related sick calls, stress, anxiety, mood, muscle tension, skin conductance, pulse transit, blood pressure, positive emotional states, wakeful relaxation
findings.source: 4. Effects of Light on the Body
findings.quote: Because natural views tend to produce positive responses, they may be more effective in reducing stress, decreasing anxiety, holding attention, and improving mood.

findings.antecedent: Windowless rooms (with view of prison courtyard/buildings, or lack of privacy)
findings.consequent: Stress-related sick calls
findings.source: 4. Effects of Light on the Body
findings.quote: inmates with windows facing a meadow or mountains had significantly lower rates of stress-related sick calls than inmates with a view of the prison courtyard and buildings.

findings.antecedent: Full-spectrum light (daylight)
findings.consequent: Human eye function
findings.quote: The human eye functions at its best when it receives the full-spectrum of light provided by daylight
key_citations: A Closer Look at Daylighted Schools, 1998

findings.antecedent: Unbalanced, narrow spectrum light (e.g., many fluorescent lights lacking blue)
findings.consequent: Improper functioning of the eye
findings.quote: this unbalanced, narrow spectrum limits the blue in the source, which leads to improper functioning of the eye.

findings.antecedent: Wavelengths of light
findings.consequent: Human body's chemistry, nervous system, circadian rhythms, pituitary gland, endocrine system, pineal gland
findings.source: Affects of Light on Internal Body Systems
findings.quote: Wavelengths of light help control the human body's chemistry

findings.antecedent: Non-visual retinal responses to light
findings.consequent: Neuroendocrine hormonal functions (pubescence, ovulation, daily rhythms)
findings.source: Affects of Light on Internal Body Systems
findings.quote: non-visual retinal responses to light mediate a number of neuroendocrine hormonal functions, which, in turn, regulate such mechanisms as pubescence, ovulation and a wide variety of daily rhythms.

findings.antecedent: Light on the skin (solar radiation)
findings.consequent: Vitamin D production, skin tanning, bilirubin dissociation, physiological disorders (if insufficient exposure)
findings.source: Affects of Light on Internal Body Systems
findings.quote: Some effects of light on the skin are vitamin D production, skin tanning, and dissociation of bilirubin.

findings.antecedent: Light falling on the retina
findings.consequent: Circadian rhythms (synchronizing internal clock to 24 hours)
findings.quote: Light falling on the retina and being transmitted to the hypothalamus controls our circadian rhythms

findings.antecedent: Prolonged exposure to cool white fluorescent lights
findings.consequent: Abnormal circadian rhythms
findings.quote: prolonged exposure to cool white fluorescent lights might induce abnormal circadian rhythms

findings.antecedent: Light absorbed by the eye
findings.consequent: Production of melatonin (affects sleep, mood, body temperature, puberty onset, tumor development)
findings.quote: light absorbed by the eye controls the production of the hormone melatonin

findings.antecedent: Inadequate daylight and artificial lighting in buildings
findings.consequent: Natural suppression of melatonin production during the day, feelings of depression
findings.quote: where daylight and artificial lighting in the interior of buildings are inadequate the natural suppression of melatonin production during the day fails and is accompanied by feelings of depression

findings.antecedent: Light entering the eye (full-spectrum)
findings.consequent: Human endocrine system, body chemistry, melatonin secretion/suppression, activity, energy level (high melatonin -> drowsiness, low melatonin -> alert)
findings.quote: how the human endocrine system, triggered by light entering the eye, regulates body chemistry, and in particular, the secretion or suppression of melatonin.

findings.antecedent: Improved interior lighting
findings.consequent: Oversleeping, overeating, energy loss, work disturbance (common subclinical problems)
findings.quote: improved interior lighting could alleviate the common subclinical problems in the population at large such as oversleeping, overeating, energy loss, and work disturbance.

findings.antecedent: Sunlight (UV radiation 290-315 nm)
findings.consequent: Vitamin D development in skin, calcium/mineral absorption, rickets, osteomalacia
findings.quote: sunlight was determined to be the key to curing rickets.

findings.antecedent: Amount of light available (outdoor light, winter, latitude)
findings.consequent: Circadian rhythms, susceptibility to Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD)
findings.quote: SAD is attributed to a variety of recurring events, but has been clearly attributed to the amount of light available for individuals.

findings.antecedent: Light therapy
findings.consequent: SAD symptoms
findings.quote: Appropriate administration of light therapy clears the symptoms within a few days.

findings.antecedent: Daylit and full-spectrum office buildings
findings.consequent: General well-being, health, absenteeism, productivity, financial savings, worker preference

findings.antecedent: Proper use of daylighting (proper spectral light)
findings.consequent: Occurrence of headaches, SAD, eyestrain

findings.antecedent: Landscape views through windows (short- and long-range views)
findings.consequent: Eyestrain, eye refocusing ability

findings.antecedent: Natural vegetation in workspace or through windows

findings.quote: Stress reduction and attentional focus can also be increased by the presence of natural vegetation in the workspace or through windows.

findings.antecedent: Daylighting (improved space)

findings.antecedent: Improved lighting conditions (high-efficiency lamps and ballasts, reduced glare)

findings.antecedent: Better quality of light (indirect light enhanced, better electric lighting installed)

findings.antecedent: Moving into a daylit building (Lockheed Martin)

findings.antecedent: Daylit Worldwide Distribution Center (VeriFone)

findings.antecedent: No desk farther than 23 feet from a window (ING Bank building)
findings.consequent: Absenteeism

findings.antecedent: Moving into a daylit building (Story County Human Services)
findings.consequent: Staff turnover
findings.quote: one group experienced a 200% decrease in the turnover of their staff.

findings.antecedent: Building renovation with daylighting (Reno Post Office)

findings.antecedent: Enhanced work environment (daylighting, personal control)

findings.antecedent: Moving offices to a daylit building (Lockheed Martin)

findings.antecedent: Office workers
findings.consequent: Value of windows in workplace

findings.antecedent: Office workers
findings.consequent: Preference to work under natural light vs. electric lighting

findings.antecedent: Daylighting
findings.consequent: Positive effects on students (better distribution of light, improved visibility, better color rendering, absence of flickering)

findings.antecedent: Natural light (skylights) vs. fluorescent lights

findings.antecedent: Daylighting in buildings (Pendergast School District)

findings.antecedent: Daylit university buildings (Center for Energy and Environmental Education, Adam Joseph Lewis Environmental Studies Center)

findings.antecedent: Natural light (skylights, windows) in store (Asheville Wine Market)

findings.consequent: Accident rates
findings.quote: accident rates dropped by approximately 50% when lighting was increased from 15 to 100 footcandles.

findings.antecedent: Natural light in warehouses (e.g., Turlock Target)
findings.consequent: Color rendering, item identification speed
findings.quote: benefits from natural light mostly result from improved color rendering. Product colors can be identified and natural light can fill the warehouse more evenly than electric lighting.

findings.antecedent: New, efficient lighting (retrofit in assembly-area space)
findings.consequent: Glare, control, interior appearance, ability to see inside wing supports, safety (shattering fixtures), ability to read measurement tools, detection of imperfections
findings.quote: The new, efficient lighting provides the employees with less glare, more control, and a nicer looking interior... one woman could see inside the 30-foot wing supports... environment is safer... read their measurement tools easier... easier detection of imperfections... by 20%

findings.antecedent: Daylighting (skylights, picture window with natural landscaping) in factory (Prince Street Technologies)
findings.consequent: Worker's compensation cases, employee attitude, comfortable working conditions, product quality, color rendering
findings.quote: an average of 20 workers' compensation cases were reported per year. In three years at the new facility, only two cases have been reported... made an immense difference in attitude.”

synthesis_conclusions: Properly installed and maintained daylighting systems are beneficial for the health, productivity, and safety of building occupants.
Natural light helps maintain good health and can cure some medical ailments.
A pleasant environment created by natural light decreases stress levels for office workers.
Productivity increases with improved worker health and leads to financial benefits for employers.
Students perform better with natural light, achieving higher test scores in daylit rooms compared to windowless or poorly lit classrooms.
Student health improves with increased vitamin D intake, leading to fewer dental cavities and better growth under full-spectrum lighting.
Daylighting benefits retail stores by providing more even light and better color rendering, leading to longer customer stays and faster item identification by employees.
In health care facilities, natural light improves patient recovery rates and allows for proper vision for the elderly in assisted living facilities.
Hospital staff benefit from the amiable environment provided by natural light, leading to calmer staff and improved patient recovery.
Productivity increases in industrial environments due to improved color rendering and better quality of light, also enhancing safety.
Daylighting decreases utility costs and improves the well-being of building occupants.
The strong influence of natural light on people in various environments makes it an important consideration for building design.
evidence_gaps: Lack of critical evaluation of the scientific nature of cited studies.
Few recent studies on the effects of natural light in hospitals.
Difficulty in isolating the specific impacts of natural light in complex healing environments.
limitations: This paper presents summary information from a noncritical literature review on daylighting in buildings. It is by no means exhaustive, and no attempt has been made to determine the scientific nature of the studies that are cited. NREL does not endorse any of the findings as the citations have not been critically reviewed.
